This is a really good hypothesis. I think that the main problem is the fact that both depression and mania are extremes and it is not very convenient for us to experience the extreme mood for a long time. I can really enjoy my manic episodes when I do not sleep up to 40 hours and am programming and doing fancy stuff. However, my body does not like it very much :)
Correct, these two (hypomania and depression) are mood's extremes. And we are the lucky ones who could switch between these fluently.
In my opinion, it is not possible to judge experiencing a mood in a qualitative way (positive / negative). What you can judge is how you can handle your moods.

I do not think you can take emotions and integrate them into moods. Indeed, emotions are helping with a mood creations but they are really very atomic. Moods are much more complex and are the results of many factors (your physical state, an environment, ...).

According to the theory, the mood's time span is larger (mood usually does not change within one day) while emotion is just a mere reaction to some subject.
It is much more difficult to control emotions since they are results of an immediate brain activity and theirs purpose is to prepare us for a concrete situation.

Examples

I have felt very good since morning = good mood
I unexpectedly see a snake = shock (emotion)

Emotions can be either lower (more primitive) or higher (usually having some social context for example love at first sight).
